text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-President Hrawi said: "Israel tries to defuse the results of 'Friends of Lebanon' conference through its daily aggressions".
-Lebanon's Drivers' Union said the weekend transportation agreement between Lebanon and Syria is not fair for Lebanese truck drivers.
-The Bank of Lebanon issues new coins in denominations of 250 and 500 Lebanese pounds.
-The Judicial authorities released two radical Palestinian guerrillas arrested last week on suspicion of firing a Katyusha rocket into Israel last week.
-The weekly cabinet meeting on Wednesday will discuss the establishment of a separate ministry of industry.
-The secretary general of the International Union of Arab Trade Unions Jammam says: "Lebanon is shifting towards dictatorship after it has been a beacon of democracy for a long time".
-A tremor shook the Lebanese coast for seven seconds yesterday.

-The American embassy in Beirut says the U.S. agriculture ministry will give $6 million in loan guarantees to Lebanon within the context of a programme to boost exports in 1997. The money will guarantee loans for the sale of American cattle to Lebanon.

-Economy and Trade Minister Jaber, who attended the "Friends of Lebanon" conference in Washington last month, says U.S. companies are eager to return to Lebanon to take part in the postwar rebuilding process.
